Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play · School & learning

award noun and verb

a prize

also prize, prizes, first prize, win a prize, award a prize, be awarded, trophy, prize-giving

classical

Verg. A. 5.70: praemia palmae
Gell. 18.2.3
Traupman 365

praemium, praemiī n.

noun, second declension

a prize, a reward

The general word for anything given for merit, a prize as much as a reward (see reward). To award one is praemium dare or tribuere (Cic. Arch. 25), to offer one prōpōnere (Caes. BC 1.17), to win one cōnsequī (Caes. BG 1.42; Lewis & Short). First prize is praemium prīmārium, second secundārium (Traupman 365).

Other words

  • palma, palmae f. — the palm of victory, first prize

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Liv. 10.47.3 (Lewis & Short); Cic. Brut. 173: cum palmam jam prīmus accēperit (Lewis & Short); Varr. RR 3.16.14: Siculum mel fert palmam (Lewis & Short)

    First the palm of the hand and the palm tree; a palm branch was given to victors from 293 BC (Livy), so the prize and the victory itself: palmam ferre, to take first prize, palmam dare, dēferre alicui, to award it. A champion has multae palmae (Cic. Rosc. Am. 17).

  • brabēum, brabēī n. — a prize in the games

    noun, second declension · also used · late Latin · Vulg. 1 Cor. 9.24 (bravium); Tert. adv. Marc. 3; Prud. Perist. 5.538 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. prize

    The Greek word, from Christian writers; Saint Paul’s runners race for it.

Examples

  • cūnctī adsint meritaeque exspectent praemia palmae

    let everyone be there and wait for the prizes they have earnedVerg. A. 5.70

  • praemium solvendae quaestiōnis pōnēbat librum veteris scrīptōris vel Graecum vel Latīnum et corōnam ē laurō plexam

    as the prize for solving a question he offered a book by an old writer, Greek or Latin, and a crown woven of bayGell. 18.2.3

  • Nescītis quod iī quī in stadiō currunt, omnēs quidem currunt, sed ūnus accipit bravium?

    Do you not know that those who run in the stadium all run, but one receives the prize?Vulg. 1 Cor. 9.24

See also reward, winner, win, competition, victory.
